topicName: Authentication & Authorization (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, API Keys)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Authentication and Authorization in REST APIs"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing REST APIs is critical for protecting sensitive data and user resources. This tutorial covers the foundational concepts and industry standards for API security, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), JSON Web Tokens (JWT), and API Keys."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. API Keys (Simple Token Authentication)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"API keys are simple strings passed in the request headers or query parameters to identify the calling application. They are primarily used for tracking usage, rate limiting, and basic authentication for public data."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"GET /api/v1/resource HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
X-API-Key: a1b2c3d4e5f67890"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. OAuth 2.0 (Delegated Authorization)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that enables applications to obtain limited access to user accounts on an HTTP service. It works by delegating user authentication to the service that hosts the user account, issuing access tokens instead of sharing credentials."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authorization Code Grant: The most secure flow, ideal for server-side applications."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Client Credentials Grant: Used for machine-to-machine (M2M) communication where no user is involved."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. OpenID Connect (OIDC - Authentication Layer)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"While OAuth 2.0 is for authorization, OpenID Connect is an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0. OIDC introduces an ID Token (a JWT) that verifies the identity of the user and provides basic profile information."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. JSON Web Tokens (JWT)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"A JSON Web Token is a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. A JWT consists of three parts separated by dots: Header, Payload, and Signature."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"APIs validate incoming requests by extracting the JWT from the Authorization header and verifying its cryptographic signature."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"GET /api/v1/protected HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsIn..."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for API Security"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always use HTTPS/TLS to encrypt data in transit and prevent token interception."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set short expiration times for Access Tokens and use Refresh Tokens to maintain sessions securely."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Validate token signatures, audiences, and issuers on every protected API request."}]
